findings.title: Immediate-cancel path leaves the WorkflowReminder row in place
findings.body: When `immediateDelete` is true, the function cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting the DB row or setting `cancelled`. This path is used on reschedule in handleNewBooking and on step deletion in workflows.tsx. On reschedule the row stays tied to the old booking with `scheduled: true`. Because cancellations go straight to SendGrid again, this path still counts toward the 100 pending-cancellation limit that this PR is meant to avoid.

findings.title: One failed cancel aborts the batch and leaves rows undeleted
findings.body: Each SendGrid cancel is awaited inside a single try block. If any request throws, the loop stops and the queued delete promises are never awaited, so later reminders in the list are never cancelled. Those emails are then sent. Already-cancelled reminders stay in the DB and are retried on every run. Each reminder should get its own try/catch.

findings.title: Cancelled reminders inside the 1-hour window can be deleted before they are cancelled
findings.body: The `deleteMany` for past-due reminders runs before the cancel step. The cron runs every 15 minutes, and SendGrid only accepts cancellations ahead of send time. A reminder flagged `cancelled` close to its send time can therefore be deleted without its batch ever being cancelled. Reminders cancelled less than about an hour before send time may also be past SendGrid's cancellation cutoff, so those emails still go out.

findings.title: Cancel query does not filter on method or referenceId
findings.body: The cancel query matches any reminder with `cancelled: true`. It does not restrict to `method: EMAIL` or require a non-null `referenceId`. A null `referenceId` would send an invalid `batch_id` to SendGrid. That error is thrown inside the shared try block and aborts all remaining cancellations.

findings.title: Scheduling query does not exclude cancelled reminders
findings.body: The query for unscheduled reminders does not filter out `cancelled: true`. Separately, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` only deletes rows when `referenceId` is null, but a row can have a `referenceId` while still `scheduled: false`; such a row is only marked cancelled. If that happens, the cron can still schedule and send an email for a cancelled booking.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation promises are not awaited
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called inside `forEach` without `await`. In a serverless environment the handler can return before the DB updates or Twilio cancels finish, so cancellations may be lost silently.
